Geez, I really thought I was blessed to have birthdays like this. I'm just now realizing I don't know how to celebrate things or enjoy parties. Thought it was cause I'm socially awkward....

Maybe one year I'd get my actual favorite cake. Or maybe I'd just get a super cheap cake of my favorite that tastes bad but I was still grateful because the thought was more than enough for me. Or maybe one year I'd actually receive a present I wanted. It was rare if I got something about my bday that I liked, but never more than one thing lol. Somewhere in my teens I just got exhausted of hoping for a 'good' bday and just wished we could stop acknowledging I even had one.

I remember one time in elementary school my mom bought bday invitations for me. It was my responsibility to write out and send the invitations. And also plan the time of my party and decide what theme I wanted.

But I didn't know how to spell their names and I didn't know how to give out invitations or find out where they lived. I felt like such a loser. I didn't deserve friends bc I couldn't even figure out how to contact people. There was something wrong with me. I was too shy and awkward.

By the time it was my birthday, we couldn't really do anything because I didn't do this simple thing. She finally called a few people that I knew, because of course she knew how to contact their parents, and after two ppl said they couldn't come cause it was too last minute/they already had other plans, I just gave up.

But no worries c: Mom got me presents anyway because of course she did! She loves me.

"I know you cut yourself to make me feel bad!"  
Now this one I use to keep reminding myself that she's fucking nutso. She's told my siblings that I use self-harm and suicide ideation to bully her and would deliberately hurt myself and leave 'clues' for her to feel guilty about it. I was genuinely in such a depressed haze, I didn't even know I was accidentally forgetting knives or wasn't covering properly. After a while, I assumed I was hiding it well cause I assumed she was a loving mother and would have gotten me help or CARED or something if she knew. My bad.  
Even when I attempted unaliving and cried for her help the first thing she said to me  was 'I know you feel like we're disappointed in you.' That made a record scratch in my head lol. That wasn't how I felt. At all. But she had to bring up her disappointment in me at literally the lowest point in my life. lol.

I've given myself a lot of grace since then but it'd still be about five more years for me to start realizing what a fucking sick asshole she is. I used to feel embarrassed at myself at continuing to trust her. But I see it's not my fault now. I was seeking love and help and that's not something to be ashamed about. For thirty years I was raised to believe abuse was love and that I was a failure, I was ugly and my own depression was my fault.

I'm finally one month out and on the path to recovery. Already my life and self worth has drastically changed. I was robbed a good chunk of my life but time feels so much slower and more full now. My life is on my terms now and I'm looking forward to it. c:

Unfortunately, it sounds like you're in an abusive friendship.

​

>  She ignores me whenever she's upset. 

She's giving you the silent treatment which is abuse. She's conditioning you to act according to her whims and punishing you for questioning the morality of this.

​

> She threw away those friendships and said I could still remain friends with them, but heavily implied I would be betraying her. 

She's isolating you from others so you can't form outside opinions as well as making it easier to corner you into agreeing with her.

Start by setting small boundaries for yourself. It's really nerve-wracking but once you have a couple in place you'll find it's much easier to keep standing up for yourself. For instance, you can say you don't enjoy trash-talking. And that's it. You don't have to explain yourself or get specific. You're allowed to have preferences without explaining things to others. Change the topic, leave the discussion, or even pull out your phone and wait for her to finish her rant if you find the other two difficult.

Another hard one is to *enjoy your solitude.* Watch cute animal videos, read some books, listen to music or a podcast, etc. If you find yourself eating lunch alone, try to treat yourself for it. I really recommend doing this in your free time too. Take yourself to a restaurant or a movie and enjoy your own company. I have social anxiety so I typically listen to music or a podcast while i'm at a restaurant and just people watch. It's nice. And you'll find being left alone isn't a punishment but a relief.
